name: Pastilla
historicNote: Pastilla (also spelled bastilla or b'stilla) traces back to Andalusian cooks who brought thin warqa pastry and sweet-savory pairings to Fez after the Reconquista, where the dish was refined into its present form. It was traditionally built around pigeon, layered with saffron-and-cinnamon spiced eggs, toasted almonds, and warqa pastry, then dusted with powdered sugar and cinnamon on top - sugar and meat in the same dish being the signature of its Andalusian ancestry.
whenEaten: An opening course at Moroccan weddings and formal feasts, traditionally the dish that announces a celebration is a serious one.
shortDescription: A sweet-and-savory pie of spiced shredded poultry, saffron eggs, and toasted almonds wrapped in paper-thin warqa pastry, dusted with cinnamon and sugar.
headnote: Warqa pastry is the traditional wrapper, but it is genuinely difficult to make at home and rarely sold outside Morocco - filo pastry, brushed layer by layer with melted butter, is the honest, widely-used substitute and is what this recipe calls for. The filling can be made a day ahead; assembling and baking is the quick part.
equipment: Wide, shallow pan for braising the poultry
Round pie dish or ovenproof skillet for assembly
Pastry brush for buttering the filo layers
miseEnPlace: Bring the filo pastry to room temperature and keep it covered with a damp cloth while working
Toast and roughly chop the almonds ahead of time
Shred the cooked poultry while still warm, discarding the bones

heat.flameNote: low enough that the eggs curd softly rather than scramble hard

steps.technique: Cooking the eggs directly in the reduced braising juices is what gives the filling its distinctive saffron-egg texture
steps.visualCue: Eggs form soft, custardy curds that cling to the shredded meat rather than a dry scramble
steps.commonMistake: High heat here turns the eggs rubbery instead of soft-set

steps.title: Layer the pastry
steps.instruction: Brush a pie dish with {0009} and layer half of {0008} into it, brushing butter between every sheet and letting the edges overhang.
steps.technique: Butter between every single layer is what makes filo shatter into shards rather than turn soggy
steps.visualCue: Each sheet is visibly glossy with butter before the next one goes on
steps.commonMistake: Skipping butter on even one layer creates a gummy spot once baked

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.instruction: Spread the meat filling evenly, scatter {0010} over it, then fold the overhanging pastry over the top and layer the remaining {0008} on top, tucking the edges under.
steps.technique: A fully enclosed parcel keeps the filling moist while the outer layers crisp
steps.visualCue: No filling is visible through the sealed top
steps.commonMistake: Leaving gaps in the seal lets steam escape and dries out the filling

steps.title: Bake
steps.instruction: Bake until deeply golden and crisp all over.
steps.technique: Dry oven heat crisps the buttered filo without drying the egg-and-meat filling underneath
steps.visualCue: The top is an even deep golden-brown, not pale
steps.commonMistake: Pulling it early leaves the middle layers soft instead of shattering-crisp

chefTips: Make the filling a full day ahead and refrigerate it - cold filling is easier to spread evenly and the flavour deepens overnight
Dust the powdered sugar and cinnamon on separately, in stripes or a lattice pattern, rather than mixed together, for the traditional presentation
donenessSummary: The pastry is uniformly deep golden and audibly crisp when tapped; the filling inside is moist, not dry.
platingNote: Dust the top with powdered sugar first, then a fine lattice of cinnamon over it, and serve warm, cut into wedges at the table.
storageNote: Best eaten the day it's baked; if needed, refrigerate up to 2 days and re-crisp in a hot oven rather than a microwave.

substitutions.impact: Closer to the traditional pigeon flavour, richer and slightly gamey

regionalVariations: Fez versions favor a finer, sweeter almond layer, while Rabat-style pastilla is often made with seafood instead of poultry
